summary:
As human space exploration advances toward extended lunar missions and journeys to Mars, astronaut health faces growing challenges from radiation, microgravity, isolation, sleep disruption, and limited medical resources. AURORA is an integrated health-monitoring and decision-support platform that connects physiological measurements, symptoms, psychological well-being, and mission-environment conditions to generate explainable health action cards.

The system monitors cardiovascular indicators, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration, mood, stress, immune-related symptoms, and available environmental telemetry, including radiation, cabin temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide.

AURORA emphasizes personalized monitoring by comparing mission measurements against individual physiological baselines in its proposed production architecture. It considers combinations of observations to identify meaningful changes rather than interpreting measurements independently.
Inspired by NASA spaceflight research on immune changes, cytokine profiles, and latent viral reactivation, AURORA includes an immune-health symptom checklist. 
Designed around offline-first operation, the proposed architecture supports encrypted local storage and secure synchronization. 
The current prototype is a local browser-based demonstration, not a validated clinical system. AURORA aims to strengthen astronaut self-monitoring and medical communication while supporting future missions beyond Earth.
details:
AURORA is an offline-capable astronaut health self-assessment and explainable decision-support concept for spacecraft, stations, lunar surface missions and future Mars expeditions. The supplied local browser prototype demonstrates manual check-ins for six health indicators, symptom follow-up, NASA evidence/context cards and a structured crew-to-flight-surgeon handoff export. The production design adds persistent personal-baseline trends, time-aligned environmental telemetry and approved store-and-forward medical messaging.

The core innovation is not another chart or a black-box “health score.” It is a traceable decision pathway: WHAT changed → WHY it may matter → WHAT to check next → WHEN to escalate. The system uses personal baselines and transparent, clinician-configurable rules. A constrained AI layer may translate evidence and measurements into plain language, but it never sets clinical severity, diagnoses, or prescribes.
